title: Pressure-cooker quinoa
subtitle: Fluffy, nutty quinoa in 8 minutes
excerpt: Quinoa cooked under pressure with the absorption method. Perfectly cooked with a slight bite, none of the bitterness of unwashed quinoa, and ready faster than the stovetop version.
sourceNotes: Quinoa is native to the Andean region of South America, where it has been cultivated for thousands of years. It became widely available in British supermarkets in the 2010s. The pressure-cooker absorption method is documented across electric pressure cooker and pressure-cooking guides.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool and freeze in airtight bags for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Cook a large batch and refrigerate for up to 5 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps refrigerated for up to 5 days. Use cold in salads or warm in bowls.

content.text: Quinoa cooked in a pressure cooker takes about 8 minutes at high pressure and produces fluffy, tender grains with a slight bite. The main advantage over stovetop cooking is consistency, no risk of it drying out or scorching on the base.

Rinse the quinoa thoroughly before cooking. The grains are coated in saponin, a naturally occurring compound that tastes bitter and soapy. Most commercially sold quinoa has been pre-rinsed, but a quick rinse under cold water removes any remaining coating.
Quinoa is cooked when the germ ring, a thin white spiral, separates from each grain and curls outwards. This is the visual indicator that it is done.

Put the rinsed quinoa in the pressure cooker. Add 375 ml of cold water (a 1:1.25 ratio) and salt. Stir once. Seal the lid and bring to high pressure. Cook at high pressure for 8 minutes. Allow a natural pressure release of 10 minutes. Quick-release any remaining pressure.

Open the lid and fluff with a fork. The quinoa is cooked when the germ ring has separated from each grain. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve warm as a side, or spread on a tray and cool rapidly for storage.

rows.cause: The saponin coating was not fully removed before cooking.
rows.fix: Rinse more thoroughly next time, rub the grains between your hands under running water for a full minute.

rows.cause: Too much water, or the natural pressure release was too long.
rows.fix: Reduce water to 360 ml next time. Quick-release after exactly 10 minutes of natural release.

content.text: Quinoa contains all nine essential amino acids. It is a complete protein, useful for vegetarian and vegan households. Use it as a rice or couscous substitute, a salad base, or in grain bowls. The pressure cooker version takes about the same time as the stovetop but needs no attention.
